review_notes: I read the whole file and the two sibling TauCeti files it depends on (the `baseChangeTowerAlgEquiv_tmul` and `baseChange_comul_tmul` lemmas). I did not run Lean. I checked the simp attributes on the tower lemmas. These are `_toAlgEquiv`, `_tmul`, `_one_tmul` and `_symm_tmul`. I found one overlap between them, in the `_tmul` / `_one_tmul` pair. The `_toAlgEquiv` lemma is closed by `rfl` and is a harmless projection lemma. `_symm_tmul` has no conflicting rule. I considered adding simp to `comulAlgHom_baseChange` and the two `_iff` lemmas and decided against it. Their right-hand sides are larger or are statements about maps, so there is no clear canonical form. The overlap finding rests on reading the lemmas, not on observed simp behaviour. In particular, I don't know which rule fires first or how `l • (1 : K)` is normalised, since I didn't check whether Mathlib has a simp lemma for it.

findings.excerpt:
baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv k L H K (1 ⊗ₜ[L] x) =
      Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k L K) (AlgHom.id k H) x
findings.problem: Two @[simp] lemmas apply to the same term `baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv k L H K (1 ⊗ₜ[L] (l ⊗ₜ[k] h))`. `baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv_tmul` rewrites it to `(l • 1) ⊗ₜ[k] h`. `baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv_one_tmul` rewrites it to `Algebra.TensorProduct.map (toAlgHom k L K) (AlgHom.id k H) (l ⊗ₜ h)`, which then becomes `algebraMap L K l ⊗ₜ h` or similar. These normal forms differ. The proof of the `_one_tmul` lemma needs `simp [Algebra.smul_def]` in the `tmul` case, which suggests `l • 1` is not simp-normalised to the `algebraMap` form on its own. Which form a user gets depends on rule priority and order, so the simp set is not confluent on pure tensors with unit scalar. The `_one_tmul` rule is also stated for a general `x : L ⊗[k] H`, so it fires on any tensor and leaves a `map` expression. Beyond the nested pure-tensor case, it competes with `_tmul` for no benefit.
findings.proposed_change: Choose a single canonical form for the pure-tensor case. Either remove @[simp] from `baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv_one_tmul`, so `_tmul` alone governs pure tensors and `_one_tmul` is used explicitly for non-pure `x`. Or keep it simp and add a simp lemma, or change the RHS of `_tmul`, so that `l • (1 : K)` normalises to `algebraMap L K l`. For example, add a lemma `baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv_tmul_one` stating the `algebraMap L K l ⊗ₜ[k] h` form for `1 ⊗ₜ (l ⊗ₜ h)`, with a priority that makes the choice explicit.
findings.benefit: Simp results for `1 ⊗ₜ (l ⊗ₜ h)` become predictable and agree between the two lemmas. Downstream uses no longer need an extra `Algebra.smul_def` step to reconcile the `l • 1` and `algebraMap` forms.
